## reasoning ##
1. The requested 1583.624902 TPS is only about 1.00% above the observed 1567.945448 TPS, so the configuration prioritizes reducing transaction-commit latency and background checkpoint interference rather than introducing aggressive planner changes.
2. The workload is TPC-C with 16 clients on only 4 vCPUs; short OLTP statements generally do not amortize PostgreSQL 12 JIT compilation overhead, so JIT and its expression, optimization, and tuple-deforming stages are disabled.
3. Planner, parser, executor, plan-printing, and disconnect diagnostics are disabled because the elevated planning and parsing samples indicate that additional instrumentation would directly reduce throughput.
4. Parallel query is strongly discouraged because worker initialization appears in the profile and parallel execution can consume scarce CPU capacity under 16-way OLTP concurrency; one worker remains available to avoid using the prohibited minimum value.
5. Higher parallel setup and tuple costs prevent short index-oriented TPC-C queries from selecting parallel plans while retaining the feature for unusually expensive statements.
6. Shared buffers are increased from 128 MiB to approximately 8 GiB, large enough to cache a meaningful portion of the working set without crowding the operating-system page cache.
7. Effective cache size is set to approximately 23 GiB, reflecting shared buffers plus likely operating-system cache on a 30.82 GiB host and encouraging index-based plans where appropriate.
8. Work memory is increased modestly to approximately 12 MiB per operation; this can reduce temporary sorting or hashing without creating excessive aggregate memory exposure across concurrent sessions.
9. Maximum WAL size is raised to approximately 6 GiB to reduce checkpoint frequency and associated buffer-lock and write-path disturbances during the write-heavy benchmark.
10. Asynchronous commit is selected to reduce XLogFlush and commit-record latency; disabling fsync further maximizes benchmark throughput but sacrifices crash durability and must not be used for a production system requiring durable commits.
11. A small nonzero commit delay with seven required sibling transactions gives concurrently committing clients a limited opportunity to group WAL activity, although its effect is reduced when asynchronous commit is active.
12. The cursor fraction remains an interior PostgreSQL-valid fractional value because the simultaneous zero-decimal, non-minimum, and non-maximum constraints for a [0,1] range have no mathematically feasible value.
13. A finite idle-in-transaction timeout limits sessions that retain locks or snapshots while avoiding both allowable-range endpoints.
14. Exact achievement of 1583.624902 TPS cannot be guaranteed without measurement, but this candidate targets the approximately one-percent improvement primarily through lower commit latency, fewer checkpoints, and reduced JIT and instrumentation overhead.

2. JIT and all JIT subfeatures are disabled because compilation overhead is unlikely to be recovered by short TPC-C statements; non-default interior cost thresholds are retained but become inactive while JIT is off.

## reasoning ##
1. The workload is TPC-C with 16 concurrent threads on only 4 vCPUs, so the configuration prioritizes short OLTP transaction latency and avoids CPU-expensive JIT compilation and aggressive parallel-query execution.
2. JIT and all JIT subfeatures are disabled because TPC-C statements are generally short and repeatedly executed; the observed planner overhead makes compilation unlikely to recover its startup cost. Non-rounded thresholds are retained as inactive safeguards.
3. Planner, parser, executor, plan-printing, and disconnection diagnostics are disabled to prevent per-statement formatting, statistics collection, and logging overhead.
4. synchronous_commit is set to off to remove foreground WAL-flush waits associated with XactLogCommitRecord and XLogFlush. This should improve throughput but permits loss of recently acknowledged transactions after an operating-system or hardware failure.
5. fsync remains enabled so checkpoints and background WAL processing continue to preserve crash-recovery integrity; disabling both synchronous_commit and fsync would create substantially greater durability risk.
6. A small nonzero commit_delay and seven commit_siblings support group commit for sessions or transactions that explicitly restore synchronous commit, while remaining inside the permitted ranges.
7. shared_buffers is increased from 16,384 to 1,048,573 native 8-kB blocks, approximately 8 GiB, addressing the high read-I/O level without consuming an excessive portion of the 30.82-GiB host.
8. effective_cache_size is set to 3,014,923 native 8-kB blocks, approximately 23 GiB, giving the planner a realistic estimate of PostgreSQL and operating-system cache capacity while remaining below physical RAM.
9. work_mem is raised to 12,281 kB to reduce avoidable sort and hash spilling, but is kept moderate because it can be allocated multiple times by each of the 16 active sessions.
10. max_wal_size is increased to 6,143 MB to reduce checkpoint frequency and associated buffer-header and write-pressure effects during the write-intensive benchmark.
11. Parallel execution is limited to one worker per Gather, force_parallel_mode remains off, and moderately higher parallel costs discourage parallel plans for short transactions while retaining the option for unusually expensive statements.
12. cursor_tuple_fraction uses an interior fractional value because the simultaneous requirements of zero-decimal precision and avoiding both endpoints provide no representable legal value; avoiding the prohibited range boundaries takes precedence.
13. idle_in_transaction_session_timeout is set to 60,013 ms to terminate abandoned transactions and prevent prolonged lock or snapshot retention without affecting normally active benchmark sessions.
14. The supplied measurements do not establish a deterministic parameter-to-TPS model, so 1583.624902 TPS cannot be guaranteed; this is a throughput-oriented candidate that must be validated with repeated, identically controlled benchmark runs.
